name: qlarity
tagline: Look at the page yourself, with a receipt.
description: Governed browser inspection for Quox dev servers. Opens a real page in an isolated headless session and answers runtime questions directly: computed styles, pseudo-element rules, DOM reads, storage. Every session runs in its own browser context, reaches only origins the operator declared, and leaves an evidence trail. Built so an agent stops guessing at runtime state and stops asking a human to paste the console.
shortDescription: Governed headless-browser inspection for dev servers
author: QUOX
marketingPoints: Answers a runtime question in seconds instead of asking someone to check the page
One browser context per session: no shared cookies, no cross-tenant leakage
Default-deny egress, enforced on every request the page makes, not just the URL you typed
Named inspectors instead of arbitrary JS, including the pseudo-element reads that catch the bugs people blame on wrappers
Arbitrary evaluation is always a human approval, never a heuristic
Every inspection witnessed through the governed boundary

namedInspectors.name: Named inspectors
namedInspectors.description: Parameterised reads that take a selector and a property, never a code string: computed style, ::before/::after rules, text, attributes, element count, bounding box, storage.

sessionIsolation.name: Per-session isolation
sessionIsolation.description: Every session gets its own browser context, owned by one org, reaped on idle and on a hard lifetime ceiling.

egressControl.name: Default-deny egress
egressControl.description: An operator declares which origins may be inspected. Redirects, iframes and page fetches are all checked, and an allowlisted name resolving to an internal address is still refused.

gatedEval.name: Approval-gated evaluation
gatedEval.description: Arbitrary JavaScript is always a human approval with the verbatim code shown. There is no probably-safe tier, because deciding whether a script mutates is undecidable.
